extension.summary: Automatically switch Kodi to software decoding by video type or per TV show, or to fix known hardware decoder issues.
extension.description:
Hardware decoding is usually preferred, but sometimes it gets things wrong, or there are known issues. Manually changing settings is a chore, so Limp aims to make that easier by automatically engaging software decoding when you need or want it, and automatically switching back when done.
You can choose when software decoding engages:
* for video types known to trip up the hardware decoder (Amlogic/CoreELEC) * automatically, for all videos 1080p and below * for any single video, from the context menu * for specific TV shows you choose (via the context menu)
Currently works on Amlogic (CoreELEC and derivatives), Windows, Apple devices and webOS. If you need other platforms, please create a GitHub issue to discuss.
extension.news: v2.0.0 - Limp is now more general: choose when it uses software decoding - for videos Amlogic's hardware decoder gets wrong, or for all videos 1080p and below - The rules now apply everywhere by default (the Apply everywhere option is gone) - limit them to paths on the new Path Limits page, with a Clear all paths button - Settings are now General, By TV Show and Path Limits pages - Add Windows support, and untested support for Apple devices and webOS - Add an option, on by default, to force hardware decoding on at start-up in case it has been left off - If Limp finds hardware decoding switched off mid-session when it is not the one holding it off, it asks if you want to turn it back on
